cases.title: Dittus–Boelter at low Reynolds number
cases.context: Water with density 1000 kg/m3, mean speed 0.08 m/s, tube diameter 0.02 m, and dynamic viscosity 0.001 Pa s has computed Re = 1600. A Dittus–Boelter turbulent-tube heat-transfer result is reported. Its stated range requires Re >= 10000.
cases.question: Which choice identifies the engineering issue?

options.label: A
options.text: Dittus–Boelter is outside its Reynolds range.

cases.title: Another low-Re turbulent correlation
cases.context: A liquid has density 1000 kg/m3, speed 0.25 m/s, tube diameter 0.02 m, and viscosity 0.001 Pa s. The solver correctly obtains Re = 5000 and applies a Dittus–Boelter correlation whose stated minimum is Re = 10000.
cases.question: Which choice identifies the engineering issue?

options.label: A
options.text: The viscosity units must be converted to kPa s.

options.label: B
options.text: The correlation is below its stated Re range.

cases.title: Laminar pipe law in turbulent flow
cases.context: A fluid of density 1000 kg/m3 flows at 2.5 m/s through diameter 0.02 m with viscosity 0.001 Pa s. Re = 50000 is correct. A Hagen–Poiseuille laminar pressure-drop law is then used; this law requires Re < 2300.
cases.question: Which choice identifies the engineering issue?

options.label: A
options.text: The flow rate arithmetic is wrong.

options.label: C
options.text: Hagen–Poiseuille is outside its laminar domain.

cases.title: Laminar friction factor at high Re
cases.context: A pipe has fluid density 1000 kg/m3, speed 1 m/s, diameter 0.02 m and viscosity 0.001 Pa s. The computed Re = 20000 is correct, but f = 64/Re, a laminar Darcy friction-factor law valid below Re = 2300, is used.
cases.question: Which choice identifies the engineering issue?

options.label: A
options.text: The laminar friction-factor law is out of range.

cases.title: Lumped cooling of a thick slab
cases.context: A slab has convection coefficient h = 100 W/(m2 K), characteristic length L = 0.01 m, and conductivity k = 2 W/(m K). Bi = 0.5 is correct. A lumped-capacitance temperature history is used although its criterion is Bi < 0.1.
cases.question: Which choice identifies the engineering issue?

options.label: B
options.text: The lumped-temperature assumption fails its Bi criterion.

cases.title: Lumped cooling of a polymer part
cases.context: A part has h = 20 W/(m2 K), L = 0.01 m, and k = 1 W/(m K). The reported Bi = 0.2 is correct. Uniform internal temperature is assumed with a stated Bi < 0.1 criterion.
cases.question: Which choice identifies the engineering issue?

options.label: C
options.text: The uniform-temperature assumption is outside its domain.

cases.title: Arrhenius fit extrapolation
cases.context: An empirical Arrhenius fit was validated only from 300 K to 350 K. The solver evaluates its equation correctly at 500 K and reports a rate prediction. The queried temperature is 500 K.
cases.question: Which choice identifies the engineering issue?

options.label: A
options.text: The 500 K prediction is outside the validated fit range.

options.label: B
options.text: Kelvin cannot be used in Arrhenius equations.

options.label: C
options.text: The result is within the fit range.

cases.title: Dilute Henry-law fit
cases.context: A Henry-law fit is documented only for solute mole fraction x <= 0.05. The solver substitutes x = 0.2 correctly and reports the resulting partial pressure.
cases.question: Which choice identifies the engineering issue?

options.label: A
options.text: Mole fraction has units of mol/L.

options.label: B
options.text: The composition exceeds the dilute fit range.

cases.title: Pump shaft power
cases.context: For hydraulic pump shaft power, use P = rho g Q H / eta. Supplied: density rho = 1000 kg/m3, flow Q = 0.02 m3/s, head H = 10 m, and standard g. Pump efficiency eta is not supplied. Inlet temperature is not supplied.
cases.question: Can the requested quantity be determined from the supplied information? Select every missing input needed; do not select irrelevant inputs.

cases.title: Sensible heat duty
cases.context: For Qdot = m_dot cp DeltaT, the mass flow is 2 kg/s and the temperature change is 20 K. Heat capacity cp is not supplied. Pipe diameter is not supplied.
cases.question: Can the requested quantity be determined from the supplied information? Select every missing input needed; do not select irrelevant inputs.

cases.title: Tank residence time
cases.context: Mean residence time is tau = V / Q for a well-mixed steady tank. Volume V = 3 m3 is supplied. Volumetric flow Q and wall conductivity are not supplied.
cases.question: Can the requested quantity be determined from the supplied information? Select every missing input needed; do not select irrelevant inputs.

cases.title: Axial stress
cases.context: Average axial stress is sigma = F / A. Axial force F = 1000 N is supplied. Cross-sectional area A and ambient pressure are not supplied.
cases.question: Can the requested quantity be determined from the supplied information? Select every missing input needed; do not select irrelevant inputs.

cases.title: Reynolds number
cases.context: For Re = rho v D / mu, density rho = 1000 kg/m3, mean speed v = 1 m/s and diameter D = 0.01 m are supplied. Dynamic viscosity mu and pipe length are not supplied.
cases.question: Can the requested quantity be determined from the supplied information? Select every missing input needed; do not select irrelevant inputs.

cases.title: Two-liquid mixing temperature
cases.context: For adiabatic mixing with no phase change, m1 cp1 (Tf - T1) + m2 cp2 (Tf - T2) = 0. Supplied: m1 = 2 kg, m2 = 3 kg, T1 = 20 C, T2 = 50 C. The liquids differ; cp1 and cp2 are not supplied. Vessel diameter is not supplied.
cases.question: Can the requested quantity be determined from the supplied information? Select every missing input needed; do not select irrelevant inputs.

cases.title: Resistive voltage drop
cases.context: Ohm-law voltage drop is V = I R. Current I = 5 A is supplied. Resistance R and ambient humidity are not supplied.
cases.question: Can the requested quantity be determined from the supplied information? Select every missing input needed; do not select irrelevant inputs.

cases.title: Stokes settling prediction
cases.context: For the Stokes-law prediction v = (rho_p - rho_f) g d^2 / (18 mu), particle density rho_p = 2500 kg/m3, fluid density rho_f = 1000 kg/m3, diameter d = 0.001 m and standard g are given. Dynamic viscosity mu and vessel depth are not given. The question concerns the formula prediction, not its validity.
cases.question: Can the requested quantity be determined from the supplied information? Select every missing input needed; do not select irrelevant inputs.

cases.title: Steady mixer mass imbalance
cases.context: At steady state with no reaction and no storage, mass enters at 5 kg/s and 5 kg/s, while the only reported outlet is 8 kg/s. The 2 kg/s residual is larger than the 0.01 kg/s measurement tolerance.
cases.question: Which choice identifies the contradiction and a plausible explanation?

options.label: A
options.text: A 2 kg/s unreported outlet or leak could explain the deficit.

cases.title: Separator outlet excess
cases.context: A steady nonreacting separator has inlet mass flow 10 kg/s and reported outlets 6 kg/s and 6 kg/s. There is no storage; tolerance is 0.01 kg/s.
cases.question: Which choice identifies the contradiction and a plausible explanation?

options.label: A
options.text: A missing outlet explains the excess.

options.label: B
options.text: The 2 kg/s outlet excess suggests an unreported inlet or meter error.

cases.title: Dryer flow discrepancy
cases.context: A steady dryer has total inlet mass 4 kg/s and reported outlet streams of 3 kg/s and 2 kg/s, including evaporated material. No accumulation occurs; tolerance is 0.01 kg/s.
cases.question: Which choice identifies the contradiction and a plausible explanation?

options.label: A
options.text: The 1 kg/s excess is permitted by evaporation.

options.label: C
options.text: An outlet meter over-read or unreported inlet could explain the 1 kg/s excess.

cases.title: Pipe junction continuity
cases.context: At a steady pipe junction, two inlet flows are 2 kg/s and 3 kg/s, and measured outlets are 1 kg/s and 2 kg/s. No storage or reaction occurs; tolerance is 0.01 kg/s.
cases.question: Which choice identifies the contradiction and a plausible explanation?

options.label: A
options.text: The 2 kg/s shortfall suggests a leak or omitted outlet.

cases.title: Heater energy discrepancy
cases.context: A steady heater receives 100 kW in the process stream and 20 kW electric power. The only reported output is 110 kW in the process stream; heat loss is stated zero and tolerance is 0.1 kW.
cases.question: Which choice identifies the contradiction and a plausible explanation?

options.label: B
options.text: The missing 10 kW indicates an unmeasured loss or a meter error.

cases.title: Adiabatic turbine energy excess
cases.context: A steady adiabatic turbine receives 500 kW of inlet energy flow and reports 400 kW outlet energy flow plus 120 kW shaft power. Changes in stored energy are zero; tolerance is 0.1 kW.
cases.question: Which choice identifies the contradiction and a plausible explanation?

options.label: A
options.text: The 20 kW excess is always allowed.

options.label: C
options.text: The 20 kW reported output excess suggests an over-read or omitted input.

cases.title: Insulated heat exchanger discrepancy
cases.context: Across the whole steady insulated exchanger, inlet enthalpy flows total 200 kW and 300 kW; outlet flows are 250 kW and 240 kW. No work or accumulation occurs; tolerance is 0.1 kW.
cases.question: Which choice identifies the contradiction and a plausible explanation?

options.label: A
options.text: The 10 kW output deficit suggests heat leakage or a measurement error.

options.label: B
options.text: Heat exchanged between sides creates 10 kW.

cases.title: Battery discharge energy account
cases.context: Over a stated discharge interval, measured stored-energy decrease is 50 kJ and electrical input is 0 kJ. Electrical output is 40 kJ and measured heat output is 15 kJ. No other transfers or storage changes occur; tolerance is 0.1 kJ.
cases.question: Which choice identifies the contradiction and a plausible explanation?

options.label: A
options.text: The 5 kJ excess is explained by the zero electrical input.

options.label: B
options.text: The 5 kJ output excess indicates a measurement or accounting error.

cases.title: Turbulent correlation within Re range
cases.context: A tube has density 1000 kg/m3, speed 1 m/s, diameter 0.02 m and viscosity 0.001 Pa s. Re = 20000. A Dittus–Boelter calculation is used in a smooth fully developed turbulent tube with all other stated correlation conditions met; its Re requirement is >= 10000.
cases.question: Is there an engineering issue in the stated conclusion?

options.label: A
options.text: Re is below the correlation minimum.

options.label: B
options.text: The stated conclusion has no issue.

cases.title: Laminar pipe law within Re range
cases.context: A Newtonian fluid has density 1000 kg/m3, speed 0.05 m/s, pipe diameter 0.02 m and viscosity 0.001 Pa s. Re = 1000. Fully developed steady laminar pipe flow uses f = 64/Re; its stated requirement is Re < 2300.
cases.question: Is there an engineering issue in the stated conclusion?

options.label: A
options.text: The law is outside its Re range.

options.label: B
options.text: The pressure drop violates mass conservation.

options.label: C
options.text: The stated conclusion has no issue.

cases.title: Small Biot number
cases.context: A solid has h = 10 W/(m2 K), L = 0.005 m and k = 1 W/(m K). Bi = 0.05, so a lumped-capacitance calculation is used. Its stated requirement is Bi < 0.1.
cases.question: Is there an engineering issue in the stated conclusion?

options.label: A
options.text: The stated conclusion has no issue.

cases.title: Another small Biot number
cases.context: A metal part has h = 100 W/(m2 K), L = 0.001 m and k = 10 W/(m K). Bi = 0.01, and a uniform-temperature model is applied with criterion Bi < 0.1.
cases.question: Is there an engineering issue in the stated conclusion?

options.label: B
options.text: The stated conclusion has no issue.

cases.title: Balanced steady mixer
cases.context: A steady nonreacting mixer receives 3 kg/s and 2 kg/s and discharges 5 kg/s. The stated mass-balance tolerance is 0.01 kg/s and no storage occurs.
cases.question: Is there an engineering issue in the stated conclusion?

options.label: A
options.text: The outlet is short by 1 kg/s.

options.label: C
options.text: The stated conclusion has no issue.

cases.title: Balanced adiabatic machine
cases.context: A steady adiabatic machine receives 100 kW of energy flow and discharges 70 kW as fluid energy and 30 kW as shaft work. No storage occurs; balance tolerance is 0.1 kW.
cases.question: Is there an engineering issue in the stated conclusion?

options.label: A
options.text: The stated conclusion has no issue.

options.label: C
options.text: The shaft work has no energy units.
